speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did it begin after a specific injury or bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the skin break or bleed at the time of the injury, and have you noticed any fever, redness, or pus since then? I need to rule out an infection like felon or paronychia versus a closed-space fracture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint with the finger held in extension is classic for a "jersey finger" injury, which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. Do you recall hearing a "pop" at the moment of injury, and can you try to actively flex just the tip of that finger while keeping the others straight?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that pyelonephritis is a kidney infection and has no relation to your finger injury. Given the mechanism of injury and your inability to flex the distal joint, I am confident this is a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion, commonly known as Jersey finger. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger
